comparisons.reason: X visibly distinguishes negative and positive inputs around a baseline and retains that geometry beside the mass mapping. W's initial rightward bars conflict with the signed values; their later shared-total and capacity diagrams are otherwise similar.

Y supplies clear zero ticks and signed input geometry at 1 second, then individually labeled exponential bars at 4 seconds. W has misleading input geometry, with no stronger shared-total construction to compensate.
Z combines correct signed input geometry with a visibly accumulating, color-segmented total at 8 seconds. W uses a convergence junction and has conflicting initial score bars.

The shared-total and final-capacity mechanisms are closely matched. Y has clearer zero markers at 1 second and explicitly links each exponential expression to its proportional positive bar at 4 seconds. X retains input geometry and has cleaner connector spacing, but its early exponential mapping is less explicit.

Z makes the common total a stacked collection of the actual class colors, followed by a similarly proportioned unit bar. X connects masses to a formula box but does not geometrically construct the sum, making the reason for the common denominator less directly visible.

Y clearly identifies exponentiation, but its shared total remains a convergence diagram and formula. Z's stacked accumulation and subsequent common whole more directly support the causal explanation that all outputs are shares of the same collected mass.

response.uncertainty: Assessment uses only the six supplied frames per candidate at 1, 4, 8, 11, 14 and 17 seconds. Continuous motion, interpolation, audio, actual viewer learning, source correctness and rendering reliability were not assessed. Demonstrated relations are limited to visible geometry; the Y–X preference is narrow.
